newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Petrogal to sell carbon unit.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Petrogal to sell carbon unit.

text.p: Portuguese state oil company Petroleos de Portugal S.A. (Petrogal ) said on Monday it planned to sell its majority stake in subsidiary Carbogal - Carbonos de Portugal S.A.
Carbogal, which has a capital of 4.6 billion escudos, produces carbon black, a raw material used to make tyres.

The board of Petrogal published a statement in the local press saying it was selling an indivisible bloc of 4,293,597 series A shares and 185,050 series B shares, representing 97.36 percent of the capital of Carbogal by public competition.
The minimum bid must be 3.2 billion escudos, it said.
Bids must be submitted at Petrogal's offices in Lisbon by 1600 local time on May 12, the statement said.
Interested parties may visit Carbogal's installations at the port of Sines in western Portugal on working days from 1-8 April by prior written agreement.

Carbon black is a black finely divided form of amorphous carbon produced by incomplete combustion of natural gas or petroleum. It is used to reinforce rubber and in the manufacture of pigments and ink.
